#### 1. congenital myasthenic syndrome 4B  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.726)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-629587)

**Proposed mechanism:** CHRNE (HGNC:2377) —DISRUPTS→ Nicotinic acetylcholine receptor assembly and function (GO:0007212); Nicotinic acetylcholine receptor assembly and function (GO:0007212) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital myasthenic syndrome (HP:0003198); Nicotinic acetylcholine receptor assembly and function (GO:0007212) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324). Loss-of-function variants in the CHRNE gene disrupt the assembly and function of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, leading to congenital myasthenic syndrome characterized by muscle weakness.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of a pathogenic variant in CHRNE that leads to a gain-of-function effect in both diseases would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if pathogenic variants in CHRNE were found to be associated with distinct molecular pathways or significantly different functional consequences for each disease, this would also weaken the proposed overlap. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism in CHRNE-related congenital myasthenic syndromes could facilitate the development of targeted therapies that address the common downstream effects on neuromuscular junction function, potentially benefiting patients with either subtype.
